summary: Backend-only regression for unified dashboard/internal-AI renewable energy logic completed (FY 2026-27 scope). 10 tests executed: 7 passed, 3 failed.

critical.issue: Dashboard GHG fuel non_renewable (228.19 MWh) does not match Internal AI combined ledger Scope1-derived value (268.19 MWh) for same FY scope, violating shared-component parity expectation.
Renewable percentage parity broken for same period: dashboard energy.renewable_pct=94.94 vs AI combined ledger result=94.488447.
Restricted scope1-only user still receives Scope2 electricity contribution (8079.91 MWh), indicating facility/scope authorization leakage in dashboard metrics path.

action_items: Investigate period/scope normalization parity between dashboard-metrics energy_service and internal-ai emissions plan for FY queries.
Enforce authorized facility scope for non-admin users in /api/esg-records/dashboard-metrics (current path only uses optional query param facility_ids).
Re-validate shared get_renewable_energy_components outputs consumed by dashboard vs AI for identical org/facility/period inputs.
critical_code_review_comments: Dashboard metrics route does not derive/force authorized facility scope from current_user; unlike internal-ai router, it accepts unrestricted org-wide aggregation when facility_ids is omitted.

Energy parity contract is currently test-fragile because dashboard and AI appear to resolve/report periods differently even for equivalent FY intent; add explicit contract tests at service level for exact same period object.
Energy service rounds sub-blocks to 2 decimals before returning; tiny-unit rows (e.g., kJ-scale) can be hidden in dashboard output and reduce debuggability for unit-conversion regressions.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the same test file and focus on the three failing tests added in this iteration: dashboard Scope1 parity, dashboard-vs-AI renewable_pct parity, and restricted-user dashboard Scope2 leakage.
rca of the issue: Reproduced with admin/restricted credentials from /app/memory/test_credentials.md. Internal AI path applies authorized_facility_scope from current_user (router.py) before executing emissions/esg services; dashboard-metrics route does not apply equivalent authorization scope and only optionally accepts facility_ids query param. This explains restricted-user Scope2 leakage. For admin parity failures, same FY intent currently yields divergent dashboard vs AI energy outcomes, indicating mismatch in period/scoping or component inclusion across the two call paths despite intended shared-service unification.
